veId":"science-reason-closing-synthesis","definitionsReviewed":13,"seriousCandidateCount":0},{"moveId":"faith-motivates-good-closing","definitionsReviewed":13,"seriousCandidateCount":2}],"candidateReviews":[{"moveId":"expected-world-evidence-of-absence","label":"Appeal to authority","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Although Shermer names physicist Victor Stenger, the move presents an expectation-based inference rather than treating Stenger's professional status as settling it. The assessment criticizes unspecified predictions and evidence, not reliance on authority."},{"moveId":"ultimate-beliefs-beyond-proof","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"accepted","rationale":"The move assigns meaning-conferring beliefs a different evidential standard merely because they are characterized as greater and significant. The assessment expressly finds no defended principle explaining why significance warrants exemption from ordinary proof."},{"moveId":"scientific-theories-change","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Not knowing what future investigators will conclude is used to support modesty about certainty, not to declare Christianity true or current science false. The assessment identifies an overextended relevance inference, not truth inferred from ignorance."},{"moveId":"many-gods-one-further","label":"Base-rate neglect","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"The move inadequately derives probability from a count of religions, but it foregrounds an aggregate frequency rather than neglecting a background rate in favor of one vivid case. Missing comparative probabilities alone does not instantiate the catalog definition."},{"moveId":"science-and-faith-enrich","label":"Subjective validation","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"McGrath reports that faith enriched his view of science, but this move's stated claim concerns that enrichment itself and does not explicitly infer external truth from personal resonance. The assessment marks an unstated truth inference, not an instantiated one."},{"moveId":"recurring-resurrection-myths","label":"Appeal to authority","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Joseph Campbell is mentioned as an illustration of comparative myth analysis, not invoked as an authority whose status settles derivation or equivalence. The assessment instead criticizes absent corroboration and comparative controls."},{"moveId":"comparative-worldviews-break-bubble","label":"Subjective validation","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"The autobiography explains how encounters changed Shermer's confidence, but he does not deem a claim accurate because it personally resonates or confirms private experience. His broader inference is under-supported comparison, not subjective validation as defined."},{"moveId":"comparative-worldviews-break-bubble","label":"Base-rate neglect","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"The move focuses on encountered believers' equal commitment without comparing actual evidence, but the assessment does not establish neglect of a known general background rate or prior probability. Incomplete comparative warrant is insufficient for this bias."},{"moveId":"ungrounded-values-reflect-society","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"The move presumptively characterizes socially generated values as prejudicial and fails to show Christianity avoids comparable distortion, but the excerpt does not yet articulate and exempt Christianity under a different standard. The defect is underdevelopment."},{"moveId":"secular-values-risk-projection","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"McGrath challenges secular values as potentially projective without showing transcendent grounding is less projective, but the move does not explicitly apply a stated evidential rule to secular belief while exempting Christianity. The assessment identifies an unmet burden."},{"moveId":"meaning-available-without-religion","label":"Subjective validation","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"The move asserts that meaningful lives are available with or without religion, but it does not treat a worldview as externally accurate because of Shermer's private resonance. The assessment distinguishes experiential availability from objective grounding."},{"moveId":"science-does-not-answer-why","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"McGrath identifies an existential question science may not answer but does not infer within this move that Christianity's answer is therefore true. The assessment explicitly treats positive theistic support as absent rather than supplied through ignorance."},{"moveId":"christianity-confronts-suffering-tension","label":"Red herring","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"The brief reference to atheism's tension is potentially distracting, but McGrath immediately concedes Christianity's suffering problem as legitimate. It does not materially divert the move away from the original challenge or leave it hidden."},{"moveId":"selective-credit-defies-falsification","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","decision":"accepted","rationale":"The criticized accounting rule applies a favorable standard to good outcomes, which count as divine action, and an exempting standard to bad outcomes, which never count against God. The assessment identifies this asymmetric treatment as the core defect."},{"moveId":"selective-credit-defies-falsification","label":"Confirmation bias","type":"bias","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Counting favorable outcomes as confirmation while discounting unfavorable outcomes makes every result preserve the prior belief. That is materially the selective interpretation of evidence described by the catalog and expressly diagnosed in the assessment."},{"moveId":"faith-motivates-relief","label":"Red herring","type":"fallacy","decision":"accepted","rationale":"Asked to address suffering's evidential challenge to an omnipotent intervening God, the move shifts to Christianity's capacity to motivate human relief. The assessment expressly says this practical point does not answer the divine-intervention problem."},{"moveId":"jesus-claimed-historically-reliable","label":"Subjective validation","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"McGrath states a personal belief in historical reliability and significance without support, but mere first-person assertion is not yet reasoning that treats truth as established because it feels resonant. The assessment identifies missing evidence, not this bias."},{"moveId":"old-resurrection-story-insulated","label":"Argument from ignorance","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Shermer asks how the resurrection is known and alleges theological insulation, but he does not infer falsity solely from the absence of proof in this move. The assessment criticizes failure to examine historical arguments rather than a defined ignorance inference."},{"moveId":"sentient-flourishing-moral-standard","label":"Appeal to authority","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"Bentham is quoted, but the substantive consideration that sentient beings can suffer is supplied rather than replaced by Bentham's status. The assessment questions the normative bridge and unresolved tradeoffs, not reliance on authority."},{"moveId":"morality-needs-beyond-us-framework","label":"Begging the question","type":"fallacy","decision":"rejected","rationale":"The need for a framework beyond individual preference is asserted without adequate support, but the move does not derive that need through premises already assuming its conclusion. An unsupported premise is not necessarily circular reasoning."},{"moveId":"faith-motivates-good-closing","label":"Subjective validation","type":"bias","decision":"accepted","rationale":"McGrath moves from finding faith personally motivating and worldview-generating to calling God a valid idea. The assessment expressly identifies the unsupported transition from personal practical importance to validity beyond imagination."},{"moveId":"faith-motivates-good-closing","label":"Belief bias","type":"bias","decision":"rejected","rationale":"The desirable motivational consequence may make the conclusion attractive, but the supplied assessment does not show McGrath judged a separate argument's validity by whether its conclusion felt believable. Subjective validation fits the expressed inference more exactly."}],"acceptedTags":[{"moveId":"ultimate-beliefs-beyond-proof","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/special-pleading/","context":"Meaning-, purpose-, and value-conferring beliefs are designated as greater truths lying beyond the proof expected of supposedly shallower claims.","rationale":"The move grants significant ultimate beliefs a different evidential standard without defending a principle connecting existential significance to exemption from proof, exactly matching the assessment's central criticism."},{"moveId":"selective-credit-defies-falsification","label":"Special pleading","type":"fallacy","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/special-pleading/","context":"Good outcomes are credited to divine action, while bad outcomes are denied comparable force against divine action, allowing belief to survive either result.","rationale":"The evidential standard changes according to whether an outcome favors God, and no principled reason for that asymmetry is supplied. The assessment identifies this selective accounting as the move's central diagnostic."},{"moveId":"selective-credit-defies-falsification","label":"Confirmation bias","type":"bias","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/confirmation-bias/","context":"Favorable outcomes are interpreted as confirming God's presence, whereas unfavorable outcomes are discounted so that they never disconfirm the existing belief system.","rationale":"The described practice selectively interprets evidence in favor of an existing belief and excludes contrary outcomes from meaningful consideration, precisely producing the unfalsifiability highlighted in the assessment."},{"moveId":"faith-motivates-relief","label":"Red herring","type":"fallacy","url":"https://logfall.com/fallacies/red-herring/","context":"In response to suffering's challenge to divine power and intervention, McGrath emphasizes that Christianity motivates believers to pursue medicine and humanitarian relief.","rationale":"The practical benefits of Christian motivation are related to suffering but do not answer why an omnipotent compassionate God permits its unequal distribution, the exact response failure identified by the assessment."},{"moveId":"faith-motivates-good-closing","label":"Subjective validation","type":"bias","url":"https://cogbias.site/biases/subjective-validation/","context":"McGrath says he personally finds in faith a motivating worldview and uses that personal practical significance to conclude that God remains a valid idea.","rationale":"The conclusion of validity is supported by faith's personal resonance and motivational usefulness rather than reality-directed evidence, matching the assessment's criticism of the move from importance to truth."}]}
